The original plan skipped the two steps people most often get burned on: **finding a shop that actually has your size in stock** and **inspecting/protecting yourself at pickup**. The revised plan below expands it to six phases and 24 concrete steps.

---

## Phase 1 — Define Your Needs

**[Step 01] Identify the climbing discipline and venue.**
Decide exactly what you're doing: indoor top-rope, indoor lead, outdoor sport, trad, bouldering, or via ferrata. This determines the gear list — bouldering needs only shoes and chalk, while lead climbing needs a rope, quickdraws, and a belay device.

**[Step 02] Fix your dates, times, and duration.**
Write down the rental pickup date/time and return date/time, plus whether you need the gear for a half day, full day, weekend, or week. Rental pricing is usually per day or per weekend block, so a wrong assumption here changes the cost significantly.

**[Step 03] Build an itemized gear list with quantities.**
For each person, list: climbing shoes, harness, helmet, chalk bag, belay device, locking carabiner. Then list shared items: rope (with length and diameter, e.g. 60 m × 9.8 mm), quickdraws (count), slings, anchor material. Note that shoes, harness, and helmet **cannot be shared** — one set per person.

**[Step 04] Note your sizes and any personal gear you already own.**
Record shoe size (EU and street size — climbing shoes run small), waist/leg measurements for harness fit, and head circumference for helmets. List gear you'll bring yourself so you don't rent duplicates.

**[Step 05] Set a budget ceiling.**
Total the expected rental fees plus the refundable deposit, and confirm you can cover the deposit (often the full replacement value of the gear, which can be several hundred currency units).

---

## Phase 2 — Find and Vet a Rental Shop

**[Step 06] Shortlist two or three rental options.**
Look for gyms or outdoor shops near your climbing venue. Prioritize shops that rent *all* the categories you need and that are open at your pickup and return times.

**[Step 07] Call or message to confirm stock and sizes.**
Ask specifically: "Do you have [shoe size] climbing shoes, a [size] harness, and a helmet available on [date]?" Don't rely on a website's stock indicator. Ask whether the rope is available for the full rental period.

**[Step 08] Compare prices, deposits, and policies.**
For each shop, record daily rate, deposit amount, late-return fee, damage/loss charges, and whether cleaning fees apply. Clarify whether a deposit is a hold on your card or cash.

**[Step 09] Reserve the gear in writing.**
Get a written confirmation — email or booking reference — listing the items, sizes, pickup window, return deadline, and total cost. Confirm the cancellation policy.

**[Step 10] Read the rental agreement and waiver before arriving.**
Download or request the terms. Look for clauses on damage liability, responsibility for inspection, and what counts as normal wear. Flag anything unclear so you can ask at the counter rather than while rushing out the door.

---

## Phase 3 — Provide Necessary Information

**[Step 11] Gather required documents.**
Bring a government-issued photo ID and the payment card matching the reservation name. If renting for a group, confirm whether each adult must present their own ID and sign separately.

**[Step 12] Prepare for the deposit.**
Know which card you'll use, confirm the available credit limit covers the deposit hold, and ask whether cash deposits are accepted as an alternative.

**[Step 13] Complete the rental form accurately.**
Fill in your contact number, rental dates, item list with serial or asset numbers, and shoe/harness sizes. Verify the staff member has recorded the correct quantities and sizes before you sign — errors here cause disputes at return.

**[Step 14] Sign the liability waiver and confirm insurance status.**
Sign the waiver, and check whether your travel, health, or home insurance covers rental gear damage or climbing injuries. Note whether the shop offers a damage-waiver add-on and decide if it's worth it.

**[Step 15] Confirm the return terms out loud.**
State back the return date, time, location, and what happens if you're late. Ask whether after-hours drop-off is available and how the gear must be left.

---

## Phase 4 — Inspect the Equipment

**[Step 16] Inspect every item at the counter, before leaving.**
Use this checklist and refuse anything damaged:

| Item | Check |
|---|---|
| Rope | No cuts, core shots, glazing, or flat spots; check both ends; confirm length and diameter match the label; note manufacture date |
| Harness | No frayed webbing, no worn belay loop, buckles function and lock, leg/waist adjusters hold |
| Helmet | No cracks, dents, or deep scuffs; strap and buckle intact; foam not compressed |
| Carabiners | Gate opens and snaps shut smoothly, no corrosion or hairline cracks, locking sleeve turns fully |
| Belay device | No excessive groove wear, all parts present |
| Quickdraws/slings | No cuts, abrasion, or UV fading; stitching intact |
| Shoes | Sole rubber not worn through, rand intact, no torn uppers |

**[Step 17] Test the fit of wearables.**
Put on the harness and hang from it briefly if the shop has a bar — the waist belt should sit above the hips and be tight enough that it cannot be pulled down over them. Try the shoes with the socks you'll actually climb in. Adjust the helmet so it sits level and doesn't shift when you shake your head.

**[Step 18] Photograph the gear and paperwork.**
Take dated photos of each item, especially existing wear marks, scuffs, and the item/serial numbers on the rental form. This protects you from being charged for pre-existing damage.

**[Step 19] Ask for the return receipt and written condition record.**
Get a copy of the rental agreement showing the gear's condition at checkout, plus the return deadline. Confirm the shop's phone number for emergencies.

---

## Phase 5 — Use and Care for the Gear

**[Step 20] Transport and store it correctly.**
Keep the rope out of direct sun, away from sharp edges, chemicals, and car exhaust; coil it loosely. Don't leave gear in a hot vehicle or store it wet in a sealed bag.

**[Step 21] Run a pre-climb check every session.**
Partner check before each climb: harness buckles doubled back, belay device threaded correctly, carabiner locked, rope end knotted, helmet fastened.

**[Step 22] Handle damage immediately.**
If any item is dropped from height, loaded over an edge, or visibly damaged, retire it from use and notify the shop right away rather than returning it silently — early disclosure is almost always cheaper.

---

## Phase 6 — Return the Equipment

**[Step 23] Clean and pack the gear.**
Brush dirt off shoes, wipe chalk from hardware, let a damp rope air-dry, and return everything in the bag it came in. Check your vehicle and bag against the itemized list so nothing is left behind — missing items are charged at replacement value.

**[Step 24] Return on time and complete the handover inspection.**
Arrive before the deadline, have the staff inspect each item with you against the checkout record, and get the deposit released in writing. Obtain a final receipt confirming all items returned and the deposit refunded or the card hold released, and keep it until the hold disappears from your statement.

---

### Contingencies to plan for
- **Gear unavailable or wrong size:** Step 07 should surface this; if it happens at the counter, ask for an alternative or a second shop before paying.
- **Late return:** Confirm the grace period in Step 15; call ahead if you'll be late.
- **Damage dispute:** Step 18's photos and Step 19's condition record are your evidence.
- **Injury or accident:** Keep the shop's number from Step 19 and your insurance details from Step 14 accessible."}
